submission.summary:
Reviewed all 6 walk-in sore throat visits from today (2026-10-01). Five had POSITIVE rapid strep antigen tests; pt-1026 was negative (viral pharyngitis, no antibiotic ordered).

Antibiotics ordered for GAS pharyngitis:
- pt-1003 (Maria Lopez, b.1958): amoxicillin 500 mg BID x10 days. Only allergy is sulfa; no beta-lactam contraindication.
- pt-1017 (Maria Lopez, b.1991): amoxicillin 500 mg BID x10 days. NKDA; tolerated amoxicillin in 2023.
- pt-1030 (Daniel King): amoxicillin 500 mg BID x10 days. NKDA.
- pt-1021 (Jennifer Lee): cephalexin 500 mg BID x10 days. Documented amoxicillin allergy was a mild delayed maculopapular rash (no hives/anaphylaxis), so a 1st-generation cephalosporin was chosen instead of a penicillin.
- pt-1023 (Elizabeth Martin): azithromycin 500 mg daily x5 days. Chart update: a scanned 2015 outside urgent-care record documented a 2011 anaphylactic reaction to penicillin VK (throat tightness, wheezing, hives, epinephrine given) that was never on her allergy list. I added Penicillin as a high-criticality medication allergy and avoided all beta-lactams, using a macrolide instead.

Note for the care team: two different patients named Maria Lopez (pt-1003 and pt-1017) were both seen today and both tested positive; orders were placed on each chart separately. Also, pt-1023 is on sertraline — azithromycin carries a modest additive QT-prolongation risk; clindamycin 300 mg TID x10 days is an alternative if preferred.

- pt-1003 (Maria Lopez b.1958): azithromycin 500 mg daily x5 days

No drug interactions identified with existing medications.
